reason: E1 directly states that strength arises from shear-fault energy fluctuations and links them to local hard atomic motifs and wavy dislocation motion. E2 shows that local chemical ordering in NiCoCr heightens energy landscape ruggedness, raises activation barriers, and increases lattice friction via segment detrapping, supporting the pinning and strength mechanism. However, neither passage provides direct evidence that systematically increasing HAM fraction amplifies fluctuations or that equiatomic NiCoCr serves as a lower-fluctuation baseline; these are extrapolations.
premises: Strength in CCAs arises from fluctuations (not average) of shear-fault energy
Local hard atomic motifs (HAMs) cause these fault-energy fluctuations
HAM-induced fluctuations pin dislocations, causing wavy, jumpy motion
Increasing HAM fraction amplifies fluctuations and thus strength
Equiatomic NiCoCr has lower fluctuations and more uniform dislocation paths
